desk.meaning: Recognizable trading workstation, software and cursor; chart updates are data, cursor is manual attention.
desk.geometry: Beveled8.8×5.5 monitor at y4.2; front screen z.22. Layered metal shell, vented back, jointed stand,9.8×5.6 wood desk, individually modelled keycaps, mouse seam, lamp and cable loops. Chart uses actual 3D candlestick bodies/wicks registered to its screen coordinates.
desk.layers: Near keyboard/mouse; screen with actual chart and rule inspector; distant wall, lamp pool and shelf. Local screen light illuminates bezel/desk.
desk.motion: One chart identity with explicit sample-time rewind for BEFORE SIGNAL. Cursor screen-coordinate travel and button depression consume notice/manual-check/manual-submit. Configuration, closing tests and status use their named events.
desk.risks: No free-floating screen card, no long unattended full-device hold, no threshold/order confusion; text must fit at screen closeups.
desk.technique: Parent the OHLC geometry and canvas UI to the same monitor. Convert price to height with (price−99.90)/0.18 × chartHeight. The screen is at local z=.17; candles at z=.225, pointer z=.50. Camera can begin in front of individual extruded candles and pull out without swapping footage. 8.9×5.55×.30 monitor, 8.3×5 screen, 12×.32×6.4 desk. Keyboard: 5×15 keys with one spacebar. Wall and lamp establish physical scale. Use original candle body height when scaling the last candle; dividing by a generic minimum exaggerates price moves. The screen painter consumes deskDisplayState; its complete serialized state is the texture cache key, including late definition highlighting and current price. test-end reveals one, two, then three historical outcomes in sequence; the monitor-end word anchor restores the chart before the camera leaves the test area. Reporting uses the shared reported flag, not an earlier opacity threshold. V5 adds .48 maximum candle depth during the opening, easing back to native .08 by frame45. Monitor geometry is the actual sharp hero group; the room and desk use the separate depth pass. Macro optics come from visualDirection.desk. V5 cursor arrivals use the spoken anchorFrame for notice, manual-check and manual-submit. Notice targets the actual last-candle center from shared chart coordinates; checking points into the condition field. The attention ring shares that candle center.
desk.lighting: Cool display fill reflects on the metal bezel and keycaps; warm point light under the desk lamp supplies a localized amber pool. Object motion changes specular response; lights are fixed.
desk.hold: Monitor shell, keyboard, mouse, lamp, desk and wall retain their transforms. The last candle follows the market-change event; only the closing shot adds a small continuing quote oscillation. No live trading connection exists.
desk.adjustable: Event frames, camera knots, OHLC data and render settings are specification inputs. Dimensions and geometry formulas above are component-library constants; changing their construction requires authoring and a new moving proof.
desk.constraints: Keep identity and numeric state consistent across builders; use global frame evaluation, no accumulated delta-time. Typography must fit at both720px and360px. Light/material changes are not substitutes for a meaningful event.

configuration.meaning: The configured condition, quantity and limit are three properties of one stored rule, not three orders.
configuration.geometry: One 10.7 by 6.5 framed transparent chart with 27 extruded OHLC candles, a 100.00 threshold, three numbered quantity cubes, and a separate 100.05 price boundary.
configuration.layers: The three configured units occupy the foreground during the size phrase; actual chart geometry remains behind them; the grounded market-record terrain extends into depth.
configuration.motion: The condition line draws, exactly three units separate, and the price-limit plane extends into depth. The same chart tilts down toward the data field during the departure. No configuration action creates an order.
configuration.risks: Do not confuse the current quote with the limit price. Do not let a boundary line cover a numeral. Wider views must contain complete context labels; close views can crop context but never the active value.
configuration.technique: Reuse bars() with the same OHLC data and price projection as the desk, enlarged to 8.7 by 4.8, depth .30. The chart is at world Y3.6. Each candle extrudes forward by condition progress with a stagger based on its index. Quantity is three .95-unit cubes with physical front plates, not a label standing for unknown size. The limit is a 10 by 5.4 translucent XZ plane placed at chart.level(100.05), with thin bounded edges. At the declared departure window the chart tilts to the ground and moves backward while the camera reaches the exact opening pose of the data family.
configuration.lighting: Warm localized key140→215; cyan fill95; metal candle edges and glass chart frame reflect their changing angle. Terrain dims under the selected properties. A real hero group uses the separate sharp foreground pass.
configuration.hold: Stored OHLC, threshold100.00, quantity3 and limit100.05 retain their meanings. Only the stated property changes presentation; no submitted or filled state appears.

data.meaning: Timestamped market updates are tested against the stored threshold. Failed updates enter history; one qualifying update leads to one instruction.
data.geometry: A 144 by 174 near field of grounded variable-height price records, a physical price-height comparison with four sampled records, three empty order slots, three stored quantity units, a fixed limit, and one assembled instruction.
data.layers: Near records have raised bodies, bevelled rims and readable atlas faces; midground records form the history; distant records continue the same ground plane. Selected price/threshold and order fields occupy a separate sharp hero layer.
data.motion: Camera skims the field, rises to the comparison, moves close to failed samples, follows the empty output, returns to the qualifying100.01sample, then follows configured values into O-01. Failed records preserve their price/time faces while travelling back into history.
data.risks: Higher cell count alone does not prove quality. Do not render a packet swarm as multiple orders. Do not keep a tiny hero centered in an enormous field. The reference lock/gripper/encryption story is deliberately absent.
data.technique: Three instanced meshes share144×174 deterministic positions: .97×height×1.23 bodies, .98×.075×1.24 rounded rims, and .91×1.17 top faces. A2048² atlas contains64 price/time records; tileUv remaps diffuse and emissive coordinates together. Heights are grounded and seeded. Selected price columns use Y=thresholdY+(price−100)×unitHeight with thresholdY3.85 and unitHeight55. The qualifying column reaches exactly the threshold at the saved spoken anchor, then reaches100.01at the event end. Failed caps transfer once to history; no duplicate source cap remains. On build, the condition, size and limit rows land separately in one5.7×3.6instruction. FORMED appears only at build completion. At the assembly first frame, source size and limit representations yield to their matching encoded instruction rows; do not show both label copies during transfer.
data.lighting: Dim warm grazing light and localized key160→260; cyan rim230→350; terrain emission dims during focus. The qualifying sample carries a warm point light. Actual hero and sky Object3D references drive the depth pass, replacing V4 empty arrays.
data.hold: Between evaluations the threshold stays fixed and the outgoing quantity is zero. Terrain light sweeps continue; the field is history, not a rising count of trades. The single order remains unsubmitted until the broker passage.

network.geometry: A23 detailed compact racks, an open optical ingress with ferrule, a transparent fiber shell,146 rings and76 lanes of84 soft luminous trails.

network.motion: O-01 contracts into the ingress; the camera aligns to the port and enters the continuous fiber axis. Native fiber geometry is reused with new global-frame timing, not the original film timeline.
network.risks: No closed cylinder or solid port backing may cover the camera path. Remove the rack only after the optical opening fills the view. No invented geographic or Tradient infrastructure claim.

Its original X-axis origin(6.2,−1.08,2.4) is translated to local zero, rotated90°aboutY, scaled1.75 and placed at world(−.07,2.23,1.05). This maps its forward direction to−Z. book.meaning: Available ask quantity changes, two units match O-01, and the last requested unit remains unfilled at its limit.
book.geometry: Seventeen ordered ask price levels, each with one physical cube per illustrated unit; two units at100.03, one at100.04which withdraws, zero at100.05, four at100.06. Three distinct requested slots stay in the foreground.
book.layers: Near requested units, middle active ask levels and deeper higher-price quantity stacks. Price labels and the100.05boundary remain separate.
book.motion: Camera approaches the best-price levels;100.04quantity leaves; two100.03units follow separate curved paths into the first two slots. The third stays an empty outline. The camera revisits the remaining unit and the100.06quantity above its limit.
book.risks: Never populate lower ask prices beneath100.03; that would contradict the illustrated fill. Requested3=filled2+remaining1. Source units must disappear only at destination contact. Limit text must not overlap its price-axis tick.
book.technique: Map price toY=1.8+(price−100.03)×50. Each row is an8.2-wide thin depth slab. Units are.72×.52×.70with a distinct face and bevels. Matching interpolates the same two row units toward the first two foreground slots with sin(pi×progress)×1.1vertical lift. A filled replacement appears at progress1, never earlier. The100.04unit translates9units outward and6units backward while withdrawing. At the report phrase, alternating rows move left/right to open the camera path through the data environment.
book.lighting: Cyan available quantity changes to warm filled quantity only at contact. Separate warm/cool practical lights expose edges and depth; the gold limit remains fixed.
book.hold: After two matches, two requested slots stay filled and the third stays empty. Remaining higher ask quantities do not drift through the limit.

report.geometry: The same order-book world opens into a clear aisle. Two execution rows assemble into one5.6×4.35electronic report. A vented8.7×5.3monitor and desk stand at Z−23.
report.layers: Near assembled report, opening order-book rows at the sides, distant receiving display. These remain one scene family across the book/report cut.
report.motion: The report forms after execution; the rows separate before the camera enters their depth. Follow R-01fromZ4toZ−23. Requested3/filled2/remaining1change together at report-return completion.
report.risks: Do not disable the depth pass while the hero is on layer1, or the report will vanish early. Do not fly through an opaque order-book shelf. Do not update the display at an arbitrary opacity threshold. Keep report captions at y1140, matching the preceding book family, while prior quantity status leaves the continuous scene.
report.technique: A shared execution builder survives the book/report cut. The two execution rows land at separate reportYpositions. reportAisle supplies the exact peel window; alternating price groups translate by9+index×.14units to opposite sides before return starts. The camera then travels through the cleared center. The actual report remains visible until returning>.99; the terminal painter reads shared reported state only. Foreground depth focus remains active and follows the same report as scale changes.

comparison.construction: Two views of the identical 27-candle OHLC sample on thin glass chart planes, each 10.7 by 5.5 with .40-depth candles, metal edge struts and shared price threshold. comparison.meaning: Attention response differs; the market and price path do not. Quantity and price limit remain the stored values. There is no outcome or profit comparison.
comparison.geometry: Two chart sheets at y=9 and y=2.1, rotations −.08 and +.08 radians; threshold at the shared bars.level(100); three .58 units. A CatmullRom route links the last candle to these units.
comparison.materials: Physical transparent glass .17 opacity, navy/gold/cyan primitives, metal rods; dense market terrain under both views.
comparison.camera: visualDirection.comparison.camera; quintic easing on global frame; pull from two views to automatic, then manual, then common chart.
comparison.animation: compare drives identical last-candle extension. automatic-action and manual-action each reveal route drawRange and three-unit instruction. no-prediction brings sheets to y=5.5 and aligns them; no-guarantee reveals future price candles. All actions are pure global-frame functions. Lower-view heading leaves at explicit labelFocusFrame2040 before the manual instruction occupies that projected area.
comparison.lighting: Warm key220, cyan fill180, studio lights at .35; hero layer1 and skies layer2. Hero focus follows the common chart; terrain dim value .85 keeps background type from competing with the action.
comparison.hold: Before manual action the cursor holds while the configured trace and three units change. After merging, future candles progress while earlier history remains fixed.
risks: No outcome comparison: do not add profit or winning directions.
Keep both charts fed from the same marketData.
The camera must fit full labels before selecting one view.
